cf.title: Fix replica identity mismatch for partitioned tables with publish_via_partition_root

input.subject: [PATCH] Fix replica identity mismatch for partitioned tables with publish_via_partition_root

verdict_reasoning: The goal of the tag fix is sound: message #3 reports a real CDC failure and the docs define 'O' as a full old row. The design is not settled. Per standards-compat-2, a 'K' tuple still contradicts the root's Relation message, which reports FULL identity. Per standards-compat-1 and demand-1, v4-0002 rejects setups that work today without a restore or upgrade plan. The stable target (standards-compat-3) also needs agreement before code review.

brief.title: Leaf-based O/K old-tuple tag under publish_via_partition_root
brief.problem: With publish_via_partition_root = true and REPLICA IDENTITY FULL on the root only, pgoutput tags UPDATE and DELETE old tuples 'O' even for leaves whose replica identity is a key. External CDC consumers that trust the 'O' tag as meaning a full old row then process data wrongly. Sawada also showed native subscribers without a key index fail to find rows, because non-key columns arrive as NULL.
brief.proposed_design: pgoutput picks the 'O' or 'K' tag from the replica identity of the leaf partition that held the old row. Message layout and relation OID stay those of the root. Korotkov's v4-0002 also rejects configurations where the leaf's replica identity does not cover the root's, checked at CREATE PUBLICATION, ALTER PUBLICATION SET, ATTACH PARTITION and ALTER TABLE REPLICA IDENTITY.
user_visible_surface: Protocol: UPDATE and DELETE messages may carry 'K' instead of 'O' for leaves without FULL replica identity under publish_via_partition_root.
Doc note in logical-replication.sgml saying the old-tuple flag follows the leaf's replica identity.
C API (v3): new logicalrep_write_update_extended and logicalrep_write_delete_extended, with the old functions kept as wrappers.
v4-0002: new errors in CREATE PUBLICATION, ALTER PUBLICATION SET, ATTACH PARTITION and ALTER TABLE REPLICA IDENTITY when leaf identity does not cover root identity.
author_claims: The current 'O' tag with key-only content violates the documented logical replication message format.
Native Postgres-to-Postgres apply is unaffected by the tag change; data applies correctly.
A client's custom CDC pipeline to Oracle processes rows wrongly because it trusts the 'O' tag.
The fix is minimal and does not change protocol structure or add behaviour.
Reviewer bahn confirmed v3 changes the tag to 'K' while the payload, with NULL for non-key columns, stays the same.
brief.thread_state: Korotkov posted v4 in August 2026, with a revised tag fix and a new DDL check, and asked for feedback on 0002. Henson Choi's question about the _extended wrappers and the native subscriber divergence are still open, and CFbot reports the patch needs a rebase.
unclear: Whether a stable back-patch is meant to include v4-0002, which makes existing configurations fail at DDL time.
What happens to existing publications and partitions that already violate the coverage rule on upgrade or restore by pg_dump.
Whether v4-0001 keeps the _extended functions or changes the base function signatures as Choi suggested.
Whether a 'K' tag with root column layout, where non-key columns are NULL, is correct per the protocol docs for a FULL-identity root relation.
Whether any third-party consumer depends on the current 'O' tag behaviour.

prior_attempts.title: propagating replica identity to partitions
prior_attempts.quote: I've not had time to work on this issue, and there are a few remaining problems in the patch; mostly that I will need to change the way pg_dump represents the replica identity so that it is only defined when the index is dumped in all partitions rather than immediately after creating the index.
prior_attempts.reason: The author withdrew it for lack of time, with work still left in the patch. pg_dump had to emit the replica identity only after the index exists in all partitions, and a bug reported by Dmitry Dolgov was still open. Reviewers agreed with the recursion; the author planned to resubmit for November.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 made replica identity recurse to partitions. v4-0002 keeps identities independent and rejects leaves that do not cover the root; v4-0001 only changes the old-tuple tag.

prior_attempts.title: Allow logical replication via inheritance root table
prior_attempts.quote: Given that, I think I need to pivot and focus on the subscriber side first. That might(?) be a smaller effort anyway, and if we can't make headway there then publisher-side support probably doesn't make sense at all.
prior_attempts.reason: The author paused the entry after finding that the subscriber side could not handle the routed data: when incoming tuples are moved to other tables, a later UPDATE or DELETE checks the root table and does not find the rows. He decided to work on subscriber-side support first. Amit Kapila also said that one extension's needs are not a reason to accept the feature in core.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P3 routed inheritance children through a parent and paused on subscriber-side row lookup. This patch fixes only the publisher tag; the subscriber miss in message #7 stays unless v4-0002 forbids the setup.

objections.title: A 'K' tuple conflicts with the root Relation message's FULL identity
objections.failure_scenario: A CDC consumer reads the Relation message for root p, which reports replica identity FULL. It then gets a 'K' DELETE in root layout with NULL in non-key columns, and matches on every column marked as key, NULLs included. The rows are still processed wrongly, now under a tag the protocol defines differently.
objections.argument: The doc hunk keeps the relation OID and tuple layout of the root, but takes the tag from the leaf. Message #9 confirms the payload does not change: b still arrives as NULL. So the stream now contradicts itself in a different place, because the Relation message describes the key columns by the root's identity. The protocol docs do not define a 'K' tuple whose key columns are given by a different relation than the one announced.
objections.author_must_show: Given the root's Relation message, how does a consumer tell which columns of a 'K' tuple are real key values?

critic.reasoning: pgoutput marks every column as key in the Relation message when the published relation is FULL, and message #9 confirms the payload still has NULL there. v4-0002 would forbid this setup, but it is not settled and 0001 stands alone without it.

objections.title: v4-0002 makes existing setups fail at restore, upgrade and minor update
objections.failure_scenario: A site runs a root with REPLICA IDENTITY FULL, a leaf with default identity, and a publication with publish_via_partition_root. After the change, pg_dump output fails at CREATE PUBLICATION or ATTACH PARTITION on restore, and pg_upgrade fails partway. With the stable target, an unrelated ALTER TABLE starts to error after a minor update.
objections.argument: Message #11 adds new errors at four DDL points, but the configurations it rejects are valid and in use today. Message #1 and message #7 build exactly this setup. The CommitFest entry targets stable, and no message says whether 0002 is meant for back branches. No message covers dump ordering, pg_upgrade checks, or what happens to catalogs that already violate the rule.
objections.author_must_show: How do pg_dump restore and pg_upgrade handle existing publications that break the coverage rule, and is 0002 intended for back branches?

critic.reasoning: Messages #1 and #7 build the setup that v4-0002 rejects, and no message covers restore, pg_upgrade or back branches. A master-only 0002 with a pg_upgrade check could solve it, so it is fixable; [P1] must not be used as support.

objections.title: Coverage check in four DDL points leaves other paths unguarded
objections.failure_scenario: A user drops the index behind a leaf's REPLICA IDENTITY USING INDEX, or creates a leaf with CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF under a FOR ALL TABLES publication. Neither path is among the four checked points, so the mismatch v4-0002 forbids exists anyway. Nobody finds out until a subscriber fails to find a row.
objections.argument: Message #11 enforces the rule at CREATE PUBLICATION, ALTER PUBLICATION SET, ATTACH PARTITION and ALTER TABLE REPLICA IDENTITY only. The invariant depends on root identity, leaf identity, the identity index, partition membership and the publication option, so many more DDL paths can break it. Any later feature that touches these paths must remember the check, and nothing fails loudly if it does not. A committer would likely prefer one place that decides the rule, or a rule that cannot drift.
objections.author_must_show: Which DDL paths can produce a leaf whose replica identity does not cover the root's, and how does v4-0002 handle each one beyond the four listed?

critic.reasoning: Message #11 lists four check points, and create table ... partition of, ALTER PUBLICATION ADD and dropping a leaf's identity index are not among them. Whether the code catches these cannot be checked from the material, so the question stands.

objections.title: Changing pgoutput wire output in a minor release
objections.failure_scenario: An existing consumer handles today's 'O' messages for these partitions, for example by ignoring NULLs. After a minor update, it receives 'K' for the same relation with no protocol version change. If it treats 'K' as unexpected for a FULL-identity relation, it errors or drops changes.
objections.argument: The entry targets stable, so the tag change would reach running consumers without them asking for it. Message #3 cites one client that gains from the change. No message checks for consumers that rely on the current output, and the brief lists this as unknown. Message #9 shows native apply does not change, so the back-patch helps external consumers only, and those are also the ones it can break.
objections.author_must_show: Why should this tag change go to back branches without a protocol version bump, rather than to master only?

critic.reasoning: The CommitFest entry targets stable and no message discusses consumers of the current output or a master-only option. The bug-fix label does not answer this, because message #9 shows the payload stays the same and only the tag changes.

objections.title: New DDL errors in v4-0002 charge all mismatched setups for a narrow gain
objections.failure_scenario: A site has a FULL root with key-identity leaves and subscribers that have a primary key, and replication works. After the change, ATTACH PARTITION or ALTER PUBLICATION SET fails, and so may a restore by pg_dump. The site finds out during a maintenance window or a restore.
objections.argument: Message #9 shows that subscribers with a key index apply these changes correctly, and only subscribers with no index diverge. v4-0002 makes every user of the mixed setup pay, but only that second group gains. No one in the thread asked for enforcement, and no one reported the divergence from the field. Message #11 proposes the check, and the thread has not weighed what it costs users who run this setup today.
objections.author_must_show: How many deployments run a root and leaves with different replica identity, and why should those whose subscribers apply correctly accept new DDL errors?

critic.reasoning: Message #9 shows that subscribers with a key index apply correctly under the mixed setup, and v4-0002 would reject that setup. Message #9 asked whether a warning is preferred and message #11 asked for feedback, so the thread has not weighed this cost.

other_surviving.title: Extended write functions add API surface with no external caller
other_surviving.failure_scenario: Core keeps logicalrep_write_update and logicalrep_write_delete as wrappers that no code calls, next to the _extended forms. Later changes to the old-tuple path have to keep both sets of functions in step, and the uncalled wrappers get no test coverage.
other_surviving.argument: Message #10 reports that the base functions have no caller in core or contrib after v3, and that these helpers are not a documented extension API. Message #11 does not say whether v4 keeps the _extended forms. Changing the one call site in pgoutput is a smaller and more permanent fix.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Which external code calls logicalrep_write_update or logicalrep_write_delete, so that the wrappers are needed?

critic.reasoning: Message #10 raised this and no later message answers it; message #11 does not say whether v4-0001 keeps the _extended forms. It is a small point, and its reviewer called it not a blocker.

refuted.title: Coverage check repeats the pg_dump ordering problem of the 2019 attempt
refuted.failure_scenario: A user dumps a database with a publish_via_partition_root publication and leaves that use REPLICA IDENTITY USING INDEX. pg_dump sets the leaf identity only after it builds the index, so the restore can pass through a state where the leaf does not cover the root. If the v4-0002 check fires in that state, pg_restore or pg_upgrade stops with an error.
refuted.argument: [P1] tried to keep replica identity consistent across partitions and stopped because pg_dump could only define the identity once the index existed in all partitions. v4-0002 adds a cross-object rule at four DDL points (message #11), and pg_dump replays all four in its own order. Message #9 and message #2 point to that 2019 thread, and message #9 says it did not end in a committed change. The thread does not say how restore order or existing violating configurations will be handled.
refuted.author_must_show: In what order does pg_dump restore publications, partitions and replica identities, and does every intermediate state pass the v4-0002 check, including in binary-upgrade mode?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which states the restore and upgrade failure more concretely. [P1] stopped on pg_dump ordering for a recursing identity, a related but different problem, so it is weak support.

refuted.title: Coverage check in v4-0002 can break pg_dump restore and pg_upgrade
refuted.failure_scenario: A cluster already has a FULL root with a key-identity leaf in a publish_via_partition_root publication. After a minor update, pg_upgrade or a pg_dump restore replays CREATE PUBLICATION, ATTACH PARTITION or ALTER TABLE REPLICA IDENTITY, and the new error stops it. The user finds out partway through an upgrade or restore.
refuted.argument: Message #11 adds errors at four DDL points but does not say what happens to catalogs that already violate the rule. The CF entry targets stable, so a minor release could reject configurations that work today. pg_dump also sets replica identity per table after the indexes exist, so a valid configuration can pass through a transient state that violates the rule during restore. [P1] stalled on this same pg_dump ordering of replica identity across partitions.
refuted.author_must_show: How do pg_dump restore and pg_upgrade behave for existing publications that violate the coverage rule, and is v4-0002 meant for back branches?

refuted.title: 'K' tag with a FULL root Relation message stays inconsistent
refuted.failure_scenario: A CDC consumer reads the root Relation message, which says replica identity FULL and marks every column as key. It then gets a 'K' old tuple with b = NULL and matches on b IS NULL. Rows are skipped on the target, with no error raised.
refuted.argument: Message #9 shows that v3 changes only the tag, and the payload still carries NULL for non-key columns under the root's layout. The protocol defines 'K' relative to the key columns that the Relation message describes, and for a FULL root those are all columns. So the change moves the inconsistency to another field instead of removing it. Changing the tag in a stable release also changes the output that existing consumers already parse.
refuted.author_must_show: With the root's Relation message marking all columns as key, how should a consumer tell from a 'K' tuple which columns are real key values and which are placeholder NULLs?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2; its stable-branch sentence duplicates standards-compat-3.

refuted.title: The four DDL checks leave other ways to break coverage
refuted.failure_scenario: A user runs create table ... partition of on a FULL root inside a FOR ALL TABLES publication, or drops the leaf index used as its replica identity. The leaf then publishes key-only or empty old tuples through the root again, and the subscriber diverges as in message #7.
refuted.argument: Message #11 enforces the rule at CREATE PUBLICATION, ALTER PUBLICATION SET, ATTACH PARTITION and ALTER TABLE REPLICA IDENTITY. It does not list create table ... partition of, ALTER PUBLICATION ADD, SET (publish_via_partition_root = true), or dropping the primary key or identity index on a leaf. Without these, the invariant that 0002 promises can be broken silently.
refuted.author_must_show: Which catalog changes can reduce a leaf's replica identity or add a leaf under a published root, and does v4-0002 check every one of them?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1. It also lists SET (publish_via_partition_root = true) as unchecked, which the ALTER PUBLICATION SET check in message #11 plausibly covers.

refuted.title: New DDL errors may break pg_dump restore and pg_upgrade
refuted.failure_scenario: A site has a FULL-identity root with key-identity leaves, which is legal today. After an upgrade, pg_dump replays CREATE PUBLICATION, ATTACH PARTITION or ALTER TABLE REPLICA IDENTITY in an order where the check fires, and the restore or pg_upgrade stops partway.
refuted.argument: pg_dump emits partitions, identity indexes, replica identity and publications as separate steps, and v4-0002 adds errors at several of them. [P1] stalled because pg_dump had to set replica identity only after the index existed in all partitions, which is the same ordering problem. The proposal says nothing about existing configurations that already violate the rule, and the CF target is stable.
refuted.author_must_show: What do pg_dump, pg_restore and pg_upgrade do with an existing database whose publications already violate the coverage rule?

refuted.title: Wire-visible tag change and new errors proposed for stable branches
refuted.failure_scenario: A third-party consumer was written against the current 'O' tag under publish_via_partition_root. After a minor release it receives 'K' with a root-shaped tuple, or the DBA's existing DDL scripts start to error. The user finds out only after the minor update is in production.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest entry targets stable. v4-0001 changes pgoutput output that external consumers read, and v4-0002 rejects configurations that work today. Message #9 shows native apply is unchanged, so the gain falls on some external CDC tools while the risk falls on everyone who takes the minor release. The thread does not say which parts are meant for back-branches.
refuted.author_must_show: Which of v4-0001 and v4-0002 is meant for back-branches, and why does the gain justify changing minor-release behaviour?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-3 for the tag change and of standards-compat-1 for the new errors.

refuted.title: Consistent leaf replica identity already avoids the mislabeled old tuple
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator who sets `alter table ... replica identity full` on every leaf, as well as on the root, gets full old rows tagged 'O' today. The patch changes the wire tag in stable branches anyway, so a third-party consumer that parses the current 'O' stream sees 'K' after a minor update. If v4-0002 also goes in, 0001 no longer changes the tag for a FULL root at all.
refuted.argument: The CDC failure in message #3 comes from a root that is FULL while its leaves are not. Running `replica identity full` on each partition is the documented way to avoid that mismatch, and it needs no new code. Message #11 adds v4-0002, which enforces that idiom at DDL time, so 0001 and 0002 are two fixes for one problem. The author treats the 'O' tag as a protocol violation, which is fair, but the proposal does not say why a doc note or 0002 alone is not enough.
refuted.author_must_show: With v4-0002 in place, which supported configuration still needs the 0001 tag change, and why is setting leaf replica identity not enough for stable branches?

critic.reasoning: 0001 and 0002 do not overlap fully. With an index-identity root and a FULL leaf, which 0002 allows, pgoutput today sends 'K' with a full old row, and only 0001 corrects that tag. The stable-branch point duplicates standards-compat-3.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: v4-0002 adds DDL errors that pg_upgrade's schema restore can hit for existing mixed-identity setups.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The patch changes what pgoutput sends for UPDATE and DELETE under publish_via_partition_root.

touch_points.label: wire protocol
touch_points.reason: The old-tuple tag changes from 'O' to 'K' for some leaves, with no protocol version change.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: see objection maintenance-fit-1: Coverage check in four DDL points leaves other paths unguarded

touch_points.reason: v3 adds logicalrep_write_update_extended and logicalrep_write_delete_extended to logicalproto.h.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: see objection standards-compat-2: A 'K' tuple conflicts with the root Relation message's FULL identity

touch_points.reason: v4-0002 errors at CREATE PUBLICATION, ATTACH PARTITION and ALTER TABLE REPLICA IDENTITY, which pg_dump output replays.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The CommitFest entry targets stable, and both the tag change and the new errors are user-visible.

touch_points.reason: see objection demand-1: New DDL errors in v4-0002 charge all mismatched setups for a narrow gain

questions: Which of v4-0001 and v4-0002 is meant for back branches, and why is a tag change without a protocol version bump acceptable in a minor release?
With the root's Relation message marking all columns as key, how does a consumer tell which columns of a 'K' tuple hold real key values?
What do pg_dump restore and pg_upgrade do with an existing publication whose leaves do not cover the root's replica identity?
Why should sites whose subscribers have a key index, and apply correctly today, get an error and not a warning from v4-0002?
Which DDL paths beyond the four listed can produce a leaf that does not cover the root's identity, and does v4-0002 check each one?

committability.owner_note: Korotkov posted v4 in message #11. The owner needs to know pgoutput, the logical replication protocol, and publication and partition DDL.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a wire-visible change that external consumers parse, and, with v4-0002, for a DDL rule that pg_dump, pg_upgrade and all later partition or publication DDL must respect indefinitely.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted revised versions through v3 and moved the entry to a new CommitFest in September 2026. The patch needs a rebase.

priority.reason: The affected setup is a publish_via_partition_root publication with mixed replica identities read by an external consumer. The tag patch is small, but v4-0002 adds DDL rules with restore and upgrade effects, and the back-branch scope is not agreed.

provisional_note: Without the code, it is not possible to check which DDL paths v4-0002 covers, whether v4-0001 keeps the _extended functions, or what the leaf lookup costs per decoded change.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: propagating replica identity to partitions
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make alter table ... replica identity on a partitioned table recurse to all partitions, and make new partitions take the parent's replica identity, mapping an index-based identity to the matching partition index. psql would also show the replica identity of partitioned tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it for lack of time, with work still left in the patch. pg_dump had to emit the replica identity only after the index exists in all partitions, and a bug reported by Dmitry Dolgov was still open. Reviewers agreed with the recursion; the author planned to resubmit for November.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I've not had time to work on this issue, and there are a few remaining problems in the patch; mostly that I will need to change the way pg_dump represents the replica identity so that it is only defined when the index is dumped in all partitions rather than immediately after creating the index.

precedents_retrieved.summary: Use indexes on the subscriber when REPLICA IDENTITY is full on the publisher

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow logical replication via inheritance root table
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets an extension or user mark an existing inheritance child so that logical replication publishes its changes through a chosen parent, reusing the publish_via_partition_root machinery. It adds a publisher-side function that tells the subscriber which tables to COPY during initial sync, and later a publish_via_parent reloption set with ALTER TABLE.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author paused the entry after finding that the subscriber side could not handle the routed data: when incoming tuples are moved to other tables, a later UPDATE or DELETE checks the root table and does not find the rows. He decided to work on subscriber-side support first. Amit Kapila also said that one extension's needs are not a reason to accept the feature in core.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Given that, I think I need to pivot and focus on the subscriber side first. That might(?) be a smaller effort anyway, and if we can't make headway there then publisher-side support probably doesn't make sense at all.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Fix bug in checking of IDENTIFY_SYSTEM result."
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Fix bug in checking of IDENTIFY_SYSTEM result."
Reverted commit(s): Fix bug in checking of IDENTIFY_SYSTEM result.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 083d29c65b7897f90c70e6dc0a4240a5fa75c8f2.

The commit changed the code so that it causes an errors when
IDENTIFY_SYSTEM returns three columns. But which prevents us
from using the replication-related utilities against the server
with older version. This is not what we want. For that
compatibility, we allow the utilities to receive three columns
as the result of IDENTIFY_SYSTEM eventhough it actually returns
four columns in 9.4 or later.

Pointed out by Andres Freund.

precedents_retrieved.title: Verify true root on replicas with amcheck
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the regular bt_check_index() function in amcheck verify the true root of a B-Tree index, so the check also works on replicas. It does this by locking the metapage and the potential root page at the same time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding. Peter Geoghegan asked what true root corruption meant and what symptom it caused, and he did not want to commit a patch that holds multiple buffer locks without a strong justification. The patch also stopped applying, and David Steele returned it after no reply from the author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Your patch looks like it gets it right (it won't deadlock with other
sessions that access the metapage), but I hesitate to commit it
without a strong justification.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reuse Workers and Replication Slots during Logical Replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets a tablesync worker, after it finishes one table, pick up the next table in init state and sync it, keeping its replication slot. This removes the cost of starting a new worker and creating and dropping a slot for each table, which matters most for many empty or small tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Benchmarks by reviewers showed regressions in some settings, and the v28 design #2 results were up to about twice as slow as HEAD and varied widely between runs. The patch also no longer applied to HEAD. Amit Kapila proposed Returned with feedback because the regressions still needed analysis, and vignesh C asked for a new entry with a fix for the regression.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IIRC, there were some regressions observed with this patch. So, one
needs to analyze those as well.

precedents_retrieved.title: Prevent pg_basebackup running as root
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make pg_basebackup refuse to run as root (except for --help/--version), matching the existing checks in initdb, pg_ctl and pg_upgrade, so it cannot create root-owned files in a data directory that the postmaster could not use. The change was not to be backpatched, as it alters behavior.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was committed by Michael Paquier and then reverted after a separate discussion that is linked but not included in the visible messages. The visible messages do not show why.

precedents_retrieved.title: Use ReadRecentBuffer() for btree root page
precedents_retrieved.summary: Cache the btree root page's buffer ID per relation and use ReadRecentBuffer() in _bt_getroot() to skip the buffer mapping lookup. To make that scale, ReadRecentBuffer() would pin with PinBuffer() instead of taking the buffer header spinlock, which also bumps the usage count.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected to keeping the cached root buffer in rd_amcache, because each access method would then duplicate the same code. He suggested putting the fields in RelationData instead. Thomas Munro answered with an experimental LRU of recent lookups, and Andres said that should be a separate facility. No revised patch followed, so in January 2024 the entry was set to Waiting on Author, and the visible messages show no reply after that.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I am wondering if we don't want something more generic than stashing this in rd_amcache.

precedents_retrieved.title: logical decoding and replication of sequences, take 2
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend logical decoding with a sequence callback, and extend built-in logical replication so publications can include sequences, so that a logical replica's sequences track the primary and do not produce duplicate values after failover. Sequence increments were decoded non-transactionally by default, and transactionally when the sequence's relfilenode was created or altered in an in-progress transaction.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why the 2024 'take 2' entry was withdrawn. They do show that an earlier committed version was reverted in April 2022. Review had found that non-transactional sequence changes could be discarded or hit an assertion before the decoding snapshot was consistent, and mixing transactional and non-transactional decoding caused snapshot, abort and streaming problems. The author judged that a fix would need an extensive redesign that was too late for that release cycle, and posted an alternative that WAL-logs sequence state at commit time.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The approach combining transactional and non-transactional behavior implemented by the patch clearly has issues, and it seems foolish to hope we'll find a simple fix.

precedents_retrieved.title: Logical Replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: Petr Jelinek posted a WIP patch set for built-in logical replication, with publication and subscription catalogs and DDL, a logical replication protocol and output plugin, and apply workers started by a launcher. It also included a proof-of-concept initial data copy, and left out sequences, DDL replication, TRUNCATE, ACLs and full pg_dump support.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The CF manager returned the entry because the newest patch was three weeks old while review was still ongoing. Peter Eisentraut had posted detailed reviews of each patch, Steve Singer had reported bugs such as a crash in the apply worker after column changes on the subscriber, and no updated version followed. Review found no design objection that blocked the work.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The newest patch is 3-week old, so marking this entry as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Test that vacuum removes tuples older than OldestXmin"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Test that vacuum removes tuples older than OldestXmin"
Reverted commit(s): Test that vacuum removes tuples older than OldestXmin
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit aa607980aee08416211f003ab41aa750f5559712.

This test proved to be unstable on the buildfarm, timing out before the
standby could catch up on 32-bit machines where more rows were required
and failing to reliably trigger multiple index vacuum rounds on 64-bit
machines where fewer rows should be required.

Because the instability is only known to be present on versions of
Postgres with TIDStore used for dead TID storage by vacuum, this is only
being reverted on master and REL_17_STABLE.

As having this coverage may be valuable, there is a discussion on the
thread of possible ways to stabilize the test. If that happens, a fixed
test can be committed again.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert analyze support for partitioned tables
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert analyze support for partitioned tables
Reverted commit(s): Describe (auto-)analyze behavior for partitioned tables; Set pg_class.reltuples for partitioned tables; Document ANALYZE storage parameters for partitioned tables; autovacuum: handle analyze for partitioned tables; Don't reset relhasindex for partitioned tables on ANALYZE
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts the following commits:
1b5617eb844cd2470a334c1d2eec66cf9b39c41a Describe (auto-)analyze behavior for partitioned tables
0e69f705cc1a3df273b38c9883fb5765991e04fe Set pg_class.reltuples for partitioned tables
41badeaba8beee7648ebe7923a41c04f1f3cb302 Document ANALYZE storage parameters for partitioned tables
0827e8af70f4653ba17ed773f123a60eadd9f9c9 autovacuum: handle analyze for partitioned tables

There are efficiency issues in this code when handling databases with
large numbers of partitions, and it doesn't look like there isn't any
trivial way to handle those.  There are some other issues as well.  It's
now too late in the cycle for nontrivial fixes, so we'll have to let
Postgres 14 users continue to manually deal with ANALYZE their
partitioned tables, and hopefully we can fix the issues for Postgres 15.

I kept [most of] be280cdad298 ("Don't reset relhasindex for partitioned
tables on ANALYZE") because while we added it due to 0827e8af70f4, it is
a good bugfix in its own right, since it affects manual analyze as well
as autovacuum-induced analyze, and there's no reason to revert it.

I retained the addition of relkind 'p' to tables included by
pg_stat_user_tables, because reverting that would require a catversion
bump.
Also, in pg14 only, I keep a struct member that was added to
PgStat_TabStatEntry to avoid breaking compatibility with existing stat
files.

Backpatch to 14.

roaster_notes.note: v4-0001 does not repeat any recorded rejection reason. The one objection is about v4-0002.
Objections were found; see the list.
Objections above cover the wire tag semantics and the v4-0002 catalog check. No on-disk format or WAL record changes are proposed.

No privilege or exposure aspect. v4-0001 changes only the 'O'/'K' flag, and the old-tuple payload stays the same, so no one sees more data than before. The v4-0002 errors are visible to table owners, but publication names in pg_publication are already readable by everyone. One thing for the design angle: a FOR ALL TABLES publication with publish_via_partition_root can block another owner's ATTACH PARTITION or REPLICA IDENTITY change.
A committer who knows the area is engaged (message #11). This lowers the doubt that anyone would own the fix, but it does not settle the objections above.
No extension or contrib module fixes the pgoutput tag. The only existing alternative is to set replica identity on each leaf, and the objection above rests on that.

The tag fix in v4-0001 has enough demand for a bug fix. Postgres documents that 'O' means a full old row, a client's CDC pipeline breaks today (message #3), and message #9 confirms the fix. The objection above covers only v4-0002.
